decisions.statement: One page is one argument, and every command taking that argument names the page.
What an argument carries belongs here.
Whether a command needs an argument belongs to that command.
Whether an argument is said at its flag or as a word belongs to the command that takes it.
An argument said as a word is typed as a bare value, and its spelling is shown only as a flag.
An argument has two spellings: `said` at its flag, `placeholder` as a word.
What an argument carries where no call and no entry says it belongs here.
An argument carrying a default is answered to every command taking it.
Every argument a command takes is a page.
A command's code reads its arguments through a type written from these pages.
A key piped into a change is no argument here.
How many times a command lets an argument be said belongs to that command.

definition: one thing a command is told on the command line
